fragments.name: Opportunity and feasibility
fragments.problem: A project can commit to a solution before value, feasibility, constraints, and alternatives are understood.
fragments.initialContext: A problem, opportunity, or change proposal exists.
fragments.resultContext: The endeavor is pursued, explored, redirected, or stopped with explicit evidence.

fragments.name: Serverless suitability, cost, risk, and provider decision
fragments.problem: Serverless and provider commitments can be made without workload, cost, risk, or exit analysis.
fragments.initialContext: Business outcomes, constraints, and candidate workload are known enough to compare alternatives.
fragments.resultContext: A serverless/hybrid/non-serverless and provider decision or bounded experiment is authorized.

fragments.name: Situational method tailoring
fragments.problem: One fixed process either overburdens a project or omits necessary controls.
fragments.initialContext: Product, risk, team, platform, compliance, and delivery factors are assessable.
fragments.resultContext: A versioned method profile selects content, evidence depth, roles, and review triggers.

fragments.name: Product, release, and increment framing
fragments.problem: Modeling can become an end in itself without a bounded outcome and acceptance evidence.
fragments.initialContext: An authorized product and method profile exist.
fragments.resultContext: A valuable vertical slice is ready with owners, risks, dependencies, and evidence.

fragments.name: Event-driven domain discovery and CIM modeling
fragments.problem: Business meaning can be lost if software/provider structure is chosen before domain and requirement understanding.
fragments.initialContext: An increment is ready and domain participants/sources are available.
fragments.resultContext: An accepted computation-independent model expresses intent, behavior, policy, and governance.

fragments.name: CIM assurance and readiness
fragments.problem: An incomplete or inconsistent CIM can propagate false certainty downstream.
fragments.initialContext: A candidate CIM revision and acceptance context exist.
fragments.resultContext: The revision is accepted, reworked, or deferred with trace and findings.

fragments.name: CIM to PIM transformation and reconciliation
fragments.problem: Automated refinement can overwrite human decisions or hide unresolved mappings.
fragments.initialContext: An accepted CIM and transformation profile exist.
fragments.resultContext: A traceable PIM draft is merged or conflicts/manual decisions are explicit.
fragments.selection: required when using the MODRISS transform

fragments.name: Platform-independent serverless architecture
fragments.problem: Serverless architecture needs explicit provider-independent services, contracts, state, integration, workflow, security, and operability.
fragments.initialContext: A PIM draft and authoritative CIM/requirements trace exist.
fragments.resultContext: An accepted provider-independent architecture is ready for capability mapping.

fragments.name: PIM to PSM transformation and reconciliation
fragments.problem: Provider mapping can silently introduce unsafe defaults or lose refinements.
fragments.initialContext: An accepted PIM and chosen supported provider profile exist.
fragments.resultContext: A traceable PSM draft is merged and mapping gaps/conflicts are explicit.

fragments.name: AWS PSM refinement and assurance
fragments.problem: Generated provider resources require explicit security, networking, quota, observability, recovery, cost, and deployment decisions.
fragments.initialContext: A reconciled AWS PSM draft and PIM trace exist.
fragments.resultContext: An accepted AWS PSM is ready for reproducible generation.

fragments.name: Reproducible model-to-text generation
fragments.problem: Generated output cannot be trusted or reproduced without exact source, template, configuration, and manifest provenance.
fragments.initialContext: An accepted PSM revision and generator profile exist.
fragments.resultContext: A generated-draft baseline and traceable manifest exist.

fragments.name: Artifact completion and test in the small
fragments.problem: Generated scaffolds can be mistaken for complete, correct software.
fragments.initialContext: A generated baseline, trace, and manual-action report exist.
fragments.resultContext: Business logic and extensions are complete and component evidence is available.

fragments.name: Test in the large and release qualification
fragments.problem: Locally correct functions and templates may fail as an integrated serverless service.
fragments.initialContext: A candidate baseline can be deployed to a representative non-production environment.
fragments.resultContext: System, acceptance, NFR, security, resilience, recovery, and operational evidence support a release decision.

fragments.name: Progressive CI/CD and transition
fragments.problem: A technically valid candidate can still fail during promotion or handover.
fragments.initialContext: An immutable qualified candidate and recovery plan exist.
fragments.resultContext: The release is progressively promoted, observed, recorded, and accepted for operation.

fragments.name: Operate, observe, control cost, and learn
fragments.problem: A deployed serverless service needs operational ownership and feedback to remain valuable, reliable, secure, and economical.
fragments.initialContext: A release has operational ownership and telemetry.
fragments.resultContext: Service/product outcomes, SLOs, risk, security, and cost are controlled and feed prioritized change.

fragments.name: Incident, problem, and controlled change propagation
fragments.problem: Emergency or evolutionary changes can diverge models, generators, code, and the running service.
fragments.initialContext: An incident, finding, dependency, or requested change exists.
fragments.resultContext: Service is restored where necessary and change is routed to the earliest authoritative source and re-evidenced.

fragments.name: Retirement, migration, and closure
fragments.problem: A service can be switched off while data, consumers, access, resources, costs, or legal obligations remain.
fragments.initialContext: A retirement/replacement trigger and accountable product/service owners exist.
fragments.resultContext: Users, data, integrations, access, resources, cost, and evidence are migrated or closed and accepted.

fragments.name: Integrated management, assurance, and evidence
fragments.problem: Lifecycle tasks become disconnected without continuous planning, risk, quality, security, change, trace, and evidence management.
fragments.resultContext: Decisions, dependencies, risks, findings, revisions, evidence, and improvement remain controlled throughout the run.
fragments.selection: continuous and required; depth is tailored
